scope: Independent source, documentation and retained fresh-build artifact review; no additional Lean process, Nanoda replay or runtime experiment started by this reviewer
semantic_review: Input is the subtype of real lists satisfying InBox Adversarial.domain; List.Forall2 enforces exactly six coordinates in the unit cube. zeroInput proves the type is inhabited.
FullHead has five rational fields; ReducedHead retains a0,a2,bias. view preserves the entire typed input and drops only a1,a3. RR is equality of views, with an actual Setoid.
fullNetwork and reducedNetwork replace only the output head in the existing actual Adversarial.original/reduced definitions. head_pruning uses the unchanged export_matches_prune theorem to bind them.

check_with_head_iff, head_certificate and all_output_heads reuse the original Check/certified_prune. This makes the existing arbitrary-rational-head corollary explicit; it is not a new pruning algorithm.

The five operation constructors add externally supplied rational values. Reduced operations discard a1/a3 updates and implement corresponding retained updates. operation_factors is proved for all constructors.

compatible_run_factors proves the finite-word statement for every operation family with an explicit factorization hypothesis. Concrete sequence_agreement and RR_preserved discharge this hypothesis for the implemented operations.

viewAlgebra is an actual Mathlib Subalgebra of real-valued state functions, defined as the range of composition with view. compatible_stable, view_algebra_stable and run_algebra_stable establish closure under pullback.
witness0/witness1 have the same typed input and retained head, differing in a1. erased_not_in_algebra proves properness; output_in_algebra puts actual model evaluation in the algebra.
badStep changes a0 using forgotten a1. The two witnesses have equal old views and unequal new views, establishing no exact reduced transformer and failure of subalgebra stability.

bad_preserves_certificate explicitly proves that this nonfactorable operation still leaves the hidden-neuron certificate valid. It does not assert that manually synchronized full/reduced heads lose static functional equality.

view_algebra_not_fixed distinguishes stable from fixed observables. erased_updates_fixed covers ignored-coordinate changes; zero_head_output/output_can_change prove actual model output can change from zero to one after an allowed bias shift.

README distinguishes supplied finite words from an adaptive policy that reads erased coordinates and accurately limits the claim to rational parameters, real model semantics and the certified raw cube.

reader_correction_review.initial_reason: Every Lean compilation succeeded; the original strict per-line axiom reader rejected legitimate wrapped axiom lists.
reader_correction_review.correction: The revised scanner consumes complete records across wrapped list whitespace, requires all nonwhitespace output to be accounted for, checks comma-separated identifier grammar, exact root multiplicities and the permitted axiom subset.

boundaries: This is a standalone instance of the composition/range observable-subalgebra construction; no PPGraph package dependency or full graph-controller implementation is added.

The theorem concerns the actual Lean real-arithmetic network definitions with rational parameters. No verified ONNX compiler, universal float32/backend equality, training or optimizer equivalence is proved.
Equality of full and reduced outputs after matched updates does not preserve an earlier safety predicate or an earlier output value.
The nonfactorability result is relative to this retained view and operation, not a proof that no richer view can execute the operation.
No MT process, Theta runtime transfer, practical superiority or scientific priority is established.
The reviewer validated existing fresh-build evidence rather than rerunning the kernel; no independent second-kernel check is claimed.
